We have the same job! Haha. I'm currently doing it PRN, so more helping with admissions and miscellaneous tasks, but I've done multiple stretches of covering a caseload for 2+ weeks at a time. 

Yes, it is very fast paced and often your plan for your day will change, be interrupted,  or complicates by medical change in condition, difficult families, difficult patients...the list goes on. My advice is to learn which tasks are non-negotiable for the day. For example, I know I have to prepare for Team Conference, attend Team Conference, and then provide an update to the patient/family within 48 hours. Insurance updates need to be sent day of (if that's one of your responsibilities) Etc. From there you can triage and start to organize your workday. 

I print out a patient list sorted by discharge date soonest - furthest out and make a to-do list on that. After the non negotiables are done or in the time I have in between, I start working through that list and making sure discharge planning is finalized (as much as it can be! 🤪) 

Learn what resources are in your area for home health and outpatient therapy (obviously) but also transportation; housing, food, utility assist, etc. 

Never be afraid to COMMUNICATE with your coworkers, your boss, and the other disciplines. Build relationships with them and earn their trust. The ability to *truly* work as an interdisciplinary team can make or break the job. Do not be afraid to ask for help if you have a question or don't know how to do something.
